text:
maria: Quick draft of a compact runbook for handling spot GPU evictions + safe rollback. Keeping it operationally lightweight, please react with :thumbsup: or add short edits.

aj: Love it — remind folks about the preempt warning window from the cloud provider (usually 30–120s). Add an explicit check for preempt signals in the agent.

maria: yeah, adding 'preempt probe' step: detect provider metadata + node taint before drain.

devon: Can we standardize the cordon/drain command we want on-call to run? Short commands reduce mistakes.

maria: Proposed minimal commands (run from bastion with k8s creds):

```
kubectl cordon NODENAME
kubectl annotate node NODENAME redwood/evicting=true
kubectl drain NODENAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```

maria: The annotation helps observability and prevents autoscaler from prematurely reprovisioning the same spot class.

ryan: Add guidance if pods fail to reschedule within 90s: escalate to infra-oncall, and trigger fallback to on-demand pool via autoscaler override.

sophie: How do we trigger override? Is it a tag flip or API call?

aj: We use the 'cluster-autoscaler' scaleUp override by patching a custom resource: `ClusterAutoscalerOverride` in `infra` namespace (internal CR). Shortcut command: 

```
kubectl -n infra patch clusterautoscaler override --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceOnDemand":true}}'
```

aj: That flips the scheduler profile; ops should monitor `node_reprovision_lag` metric.

maria: Escalation path (short):
- T+0: cordon & annotate (on-call)
- T+0..30s: drain and monitor pod reschedules (check `kubectl get pods -o wide`)
- T+90s: if >10% of GPU pods unscheduled, alert infra-oncall and run autoscaler override
- T+300s: if still degraded, page SRE lead (pagerduty: infra-sre) and open incident channel `#inc-spot-eviction`

devon: Also include runbook note about node taints for graceful drain: we add `node.kubernetes.io/spot-eviction=true:NoSchedule` when metadata signals imminent termination so new pods don't land there.

maria: Observability checks to keep in the runbook:
- spot_eviction_rate (1m / 5m)
- unschedulable_gpu_pods_count
- node_reprovision_lag_seconds
- cluster_cpu_pressure (so we don't cause cascading OOMs)

kube-bot: [automated] detected 1 spot termination warning on ip-10-0-23-45.us-west-2; preempt window 90s.

ryan: If automation detects a preempt warning: auto-annotate + cordon, kick graceful eviction pipeline. Only page humans if autoscale override needed.

aj: Add cost-control guidance: we accept short-term interruptions for background batch jobs. For latency SLAs, prefer pinned on-demand or dedicated pools. Recommend cost guardrail: if spot_eviction_rate > 0.05 for 1h, switch more traffic to dedicated.

maria: Final quick checklist for on-call message (copy/paste into channel):

```
1) cordon NODENAME
2) annotate node NODENAME redwood/evicting=true
3) drain NODENAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
4) monitor pods: kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep NODENAME
5) if unscheduled > 10% after 90s: patch ClusterAutoscaler override
6) page infra-oncall -> infra-sre if >5m degraded
```

devon: This is great. Suggest we also add a one-line owner for each step in the doc and a quick rollback command for the override.

maria: Will add owners + rollback snippet: `kubectl -n infra patch clusterautoscaler override --type merge -p '{"spec":{"forceOnDemand":false}}'`

sophie: thumbs up. can we also add a small note about prewarming on-demand pool for large-scale evictions? prewarm = keep 2 reserve nodes during business hours.

maria: good call. adding reserve pool recommendation + runbook link to Dedicated provisioning page. I'll convert this thread into a short runbook in the ops repo and ping the SRE weekly sync. :white_check_mark:
